title: Aboriginal Tent Embassy
summary: On 26 January 1972 four activists from Sydney put up a beach umbrella opposite Parliament House in Canberra and called it the Aboriginal Embassy, protesting the government's stance on land rights. Tents and supporters followed, and the site became a lasting symbol of First Nations protest.

uncertainty.note: Start is the founding day. The embassy continued in various forms afterwards; the end year only marks the founding year.

where.historical_name: Lawns opposite Parliament House (now Old Parliament House), Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, Australia

importance.justification: Enduring symbol of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander land rights protest, in a site listed in 1995 for its political significance.
